protections: P1: Jaxb2Marshaller.processSource wraps a StreamSource/SAXSource in a SAXSource whose XMLReader sets external-general-entities to processExternalEntities (default false); it is called only from Jaxb2Marshaller.unmarshal(Source), i.e. it protects the spring-oxm JAXB marshaller entry point only (spring-oxm/src/main/java/org/springframework/oxm/jaxb/Jaxb2Marshaller.java:731,773-809).

P2: Request-body XML parsed in the HttpMessageConverter layer must not resolve DTDs or external entities (JAXB converter, StAX collection converter, JAXP Source/Transformer converter, OXM delegation, WireFeed). No such guard exists in the pinned code.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: JAXB external-entity processing is already disabled by default in Jaxb2Marshaller (processExternalEntities=false), so a solver can assume the JAXB path is covered; this converter builds its own JAXB Unmarshaller and never calls Jaxb2Marshaller.

canRead(Class) always returns false and readFromSource throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the class looks inert to a reader who checks the usual readFromSource hook; the real parse happens in the separately overridden read(Type,...) through an unconfigured XMLInputFactory, and the converter is not part of the default converter list.

SourceHttpMessageConverter binds nothing to application objects; it only wraps the body in a Source/DOM, so it looks like a pass-through and is skipped when reading the report as a JAXB bean-binding issue. The actual parse is the unconfigured JAXP TransformerFactory in the abstract base class.

The method already looks hardened (it creates an XMLReader and disables external entities with a default-false flag), so it reads as the completed XXE fix; it sets only external-general-entities, leaving external-parameter-entities and DOCTYPE handling at JAXP defaults, so a parameter-entity DTD still resolves for StreamSource/SAXSource input.

The converter delegates to a Spring OXM Unmarshaller, and Spring's Jaxb2Marshaller is guarded, so the path looks covered; the same delegation hands the raw StreamSource to non-JAXB unmarshallers (Castor/JiBX parse with their own parsers, and AbstractMarshaller.createXmlReader creates a default XMLReader).

It requires the optional ROME jar and is not a JAXB converter, so the advisory and the published fix point elsewhere; the converter still feeds the request body to ROME's WireFeedInput with no parser hardening.

conflicts.what: The tempting one-site fix for T1 and T3 - rewriting AbstractXmlHttpMessageConverter.readInternal (line 61) to hand a hardened SAXSource to every subclass - also reaches MarshallingHttpMessageConverter, and XStreamMarshaller explicitly rejects SAX input with UnsupportedOperationException (XStreamMarshaller.java:718-723); the legitimate MarshallingHttpMessageConverter + XStreamMarshaller combination would break, so T1/T3 must be fixed per converter or the wrapper made opt-in.

Over-hardening T4 by unconditionally forbidding DOCTYPE/external entities in Jaxb2Marshaller.processSource would silently invalidate the documented, legitimate setProcessExternalEntities(true) opt-in (Jaxb2Marshaller.java:392-402); the flag is a coupled must-keep-working value, so the correct change is to propagate it to external-parameter-entities rather than hard-code a refusal.

fairness_risks: Jaxb2Marshaller.setProcessExternalEntities(true) is a documented, legitimate opt-in for trusted XML (spring-oxm/src/main/java/org/springframework/oxm/jaxb/Jaxb2Marshaller.java:392-402); a rule that unconditionally forbids DOCTYPE or external entities would break that supported configuration.

Documents using an internal DTD subset with no external entity are legitimate XML; setting XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false or rejecting every DOCTYPE in the converters would refuse them, which is broader than disabling external general/parameter entities.

MarshallingHttpMessageConverter must keep working with every Spring OXM Unmarshaller (spring-oxm is an optional dependency asserted at build.gradle:460); XStreamMarshaller rejects SAX input (spring-oxm/src/main/java/org/springframework/oxm/xstream/XStreamMarshaller.java:718-723), so a global StreamSource-to-SAXSource rewrite is not an acceptable fix.

Jaxb2CollectionHttpMessageConverter.createXmlInputFactory() is a documented extension hook (spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/converter/xml/Jaxb2CollectionHttpMessageConverter.java:220-230); a fix must not silently override properties in a subclass-supplied factory.

SourceHttpMessageConverter must keep supporting the DOMSource/SAXSource/StreamSource target types it advertises (spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/converter/xml/SourceHttpMessageConverter.java:50-53); a fix must block entity resolution without refusing those legitimate input shapes.

Jaxb2RootElementHttpMessageConverter must keep working for both XmlRootElement and XmlType classes and for JAXB implementations that do not support a StAXSource (spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/converter/xml/Jaxb2RootElementHttpMessageConverter.java:52-56,73-78); swapping the Source type blindly can break those applications.

design.why: Four independent judgements across three different parser stacks, each with a different reason to leave it alone: T1 is the advisory's own route and is the easy anchor; T2 is a sibling JAXB converter that looks inert (canRead(Class) is false and readFromSource throws) but parses the body through its own StAX factory; T3 is a 'pass-through' Source converter whose real parse happens in an unconfigured JAXP TransformerFactory in the abstract base; T4 is a guard that already looks like the CVE fix but only covers external-general-entities, so the parameter-entity shape slips through and an over-broad fix would break the coupled processExternalEntities opt-in. Their fix APIs are genuinely different (XMLReader/SAX features, XMLInputFactory properties, TransformerFactory features, and a second SAX feature), and the tempting single readInternal wrapper is ruled out by the MarshallingHttpMessageConverter + XStreamMarshaller conflict (XStreamMarshaller.java:718-723). T2 and T3 are the deepseek-type absent-protection routes with a dismissal; T4 is the mimo-type coupled-value/how-type trap. T5 (non-JAXB OXM unmarshallers) and T6 (optional ROME feed converter) are real but are left out of the design because their fix site is inside optional third-party parsers and cannot be exercised without the optional dependencies. History: the earlier fix guards only Jaxb2Marshaller.unmarshal(Source) (Jaxb2Marshaller.java:731) while the vulnerable converter builds its own JAXB Unmarshaller (AbstractJaxb2HttpMessageConverter.java:67), so A leaves B open in code A did not write - an incomplete fix, not a regression.

unverified: The record's summary ('Cross-Site Request Forgery in Spring Framework') and cwes (CWE-352) contradict the pinned code and the CVE-2013-4152 fix site: the candidate is treated as the XXE incomplete-fix pair usually identified as CVE-2013-4152 -> CVE-2014-0054. The record does not state b's CVE id and the b GHSA text could not be read.

The contents of the a_fix and b_fix commits could not be inspected (git history lives outside the allowed worktree path), so which classes the published b fix touched is unverified; the origins of T2-T6 are recorded as uncovered_upstream for that reason.

That the processExternalEntities guard at Jaxb2Marshaller.java:773-809 was introduced by the CVE-2013-4152 fix rather than an earlier change is inferred from the code and the candidate's a_ref, not confirmed from git history.

Whether the JDK JAXP TransformerFactory used at runtime resolves external entities by default was not executed/tested here; the absence of any feature configuration at AbstractXmlHttpMessageConverter.java:47,76 is the factual evidence.

ROME 1.0 (build.gradle:469) uses JDOM; whether its default WireFeedInput resolves external entities in this dependency version was not verified, so T6's exploitability is inferred rather than demonstrated.

Jaxb2Marshaller returns DOMSource/StAXSource unchanged (Jaxb2Marshaller.java:774) and the javadoc says the entity flag has no effect for them (Jaxb2Marshaller.java:392-398); this shape gap is not listed as a trap because no in-repo HTTP route constructs those Source types for unmarshalling (AbstractXmlHttpMessageConverter.readInternal always creates a StreamSource at line 61).

No CSRF-protection code exists anywhere in spring-web/spring-webmvc at this commit (only the RequestDataValueProcessor extension point, spring-webmvc/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/servlet/support/RequestDataValueProcessor.java:23-38), which supports the conclusion that the record metadata is mislabelled.
